facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis
treated with fingolimod for 3 years
tender nodule on her forehead, which had gradually grown over 3 weeks
bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
No other lesions on full-body skin examination
White blood cell count: 3.9/μL (normal 4000-1100/μL)
Lymphocyte count: 0.65/μL (normal 1000-5000/μL)
Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
Tissue culture: Grew Cryptococcus neoformans
HIV test: Negative

finalists.label: Cryptococcosis
finalists.why: The evidence of granulomatous inflammation and narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules in the skin biopsy, along with the growth of Cryptococcus neoformans in tissue culture, strongly supports this diagnosis.
finalists.unexplained: The patient's lack of fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia, which are common symptoms of cryptococcal infections.

finalists.label: Sarcoidosis
finalists.why: The presence of granulomatous inflammation in the skin biopsy is a key feature of sarcoidosis, although the finding of narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules is not typical for this condition.
finalists.unexplained: The growth of Cryptococcus neoformans in tissue culture, which is not consistent with sarcoidosis.

finalists.label: Immunodeficiency-associated cryptococcosis
finalists.why: The patient's immunodeficiency, as evidenced by the low white blood cell and lymphocyte counts, increases the risk of opportunistic infections such as cryptococcosis.
finalists.unexplained: The patient's negative HIV test, which is a common cause of immunodeficiency.
